tier_reason: The README table (2026-03-04 run of examples/quantizer_comparison.rs) compares zenquant with imagequant 4, quantette 0.5, quantizr and color_quant, and every number in claimed_speedup matches it; the harness code and competitor versions are public, but no CPU model, OS or rustc version is recorded for the run (benchmarks/README.md only asks future runs to record them), and the ~ms column comes from the approximate multi-threaded mode, so first-party tier C.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 2 GitHub stars; crates.io zenquant 0.1.3 (8,680 downloads, 4,077 recent); default quantizer in zenpng, zengif, zenwebp (all imazen's own crates)
corrections.caveats: Not faster than the incumbents in the README table: zenquant Best takes the same ~542 ms as imagequant s1 d100 and the Fast preset (321 ms) only ties imagequant s4 (315 ms) and loses to quantette k-means (265 ms); the win is file size and butteraugli, while quantette leads SSIMULACRA2/DSSIM. The ~ms column comes from the default run, which times a single run per image while 8 images are quantized in parallel threads, reuses cached per-image results (and their timings) unless --recalc is passed, and is described by the repo's own benchmarks/README.md as 'fine for the quality columns, not for timing claims'; the single-thread --benchmark mode has no committed result. Even in --benchmark mode the comparison is not single-core for every contender: imagequant 4 is a dev-dependency with default features, which enable its rayon 'threads' feature, while zenquant is no_std and single-threaded; imagequant's timed closure also includes an RGB-to-RGBA copy. No CPU, RAM, OS or rustc version is recorded for the 2026-03-04 run. Evidence is first-party, the README notes AI-generated code ('Not all code manually reviewed'), and the repo manifest is at 0.1.4 while crates.io still serves 0.1.3. Licence is dual (AGPL-3.0-only OR commercial; 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 were AGPL-3.0-or-later), so the AGPL branch is copyable but with network copyleft.

notes: Record is accurate; this is a quality/size entry, not a speed win, so the orchestrator should file the not-faster shortcoming. Harness flaws to record: approximate multi-threaded timing with cached results, imagequant allowed its internal rayon threads, no hardware or rustc recorded, 2 stars.

tier_reason: The README Performance table lists only honeydiff's own timings (2.81, 2.18, 147, 4.34, 14.7, 10.9 ms, matching the record) with no other library timed, no harness in the repo, and the linked benchmarks/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md returns 404; with no baseline comparison anywhere, D is the right tier.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 14 stars, 0 forks, 19 commits (release-tag commits only); npm @vizzly-testing/honeydiff 0.17.0
corrections.caveats: The public repo holds only the JS loader (index.js, load-platform.cjs), type definitions, examples, assets and release metadata; the Rust engine source is not here (README's Development section says cargo build --release, but Cargo.toml and src/ return 404, and package.json's repository field points to vizzly-testing/r-honeydiff, which returns 404), so the MIT licence cannot be exercised on the engine code. README links benchmarks/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md, which also returns 404. The 'current local benchmark snapshots' state no hardware, flags or harness; the CHANGELOG has self-comparisons only (0.8.1: SSIM 239 ms to 51 ms at 1920x1080, 35 ms to 8.3 ms at 640x480; 0.11.1: Criterion runs 'on Apple Silicon', tall screenshot ~192 ms default and ~4.1 ms exact/no-AA), and the 0.8.1 SSIM figures predate the 0.11.0 metric correctness change that made SSIM Gaussian-weighted and slowed the hot paths. No comparison against odiff, pixelmatch or any other diff tool; web searches in the earlier pass found no third-party honeydiff benchmark. Low notability (14 stars).

notes: Kept at D per the keep-and-document rule (no baseline comparison, not notable, binary-only repo); nothing is invalid or fabricated. Shortcomings to record: no source in the public repo, no baseline, benchmark doc 404, 14 stars.

tier_reason: No published numbers against OpenCV or libyuv: the README describes only a self-comparison test mode (scalar vs SIMD), src/Test/TestResize.cpp holds an optional SIMD_OPENCV ResizeOpenCvSpecialTest that times cv::resize against Simd::Resize on a BGR24 480x640 to 333x444 image but no output is committed, and the docs (release notes 2013-2026, Doxygen help) carry no timing tables.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 2.3k stars, 456 forks; vcpkg port; proposed as an OpenCV replacement in wpilibsuite/allwpilib issue 7108 (no numbers)
corrections.caveats: Claim-only: no Simd versus OpenCV or libyuv numbers are published anywhere reachable. The project site ermig1979.github.io/Simd is EGRESS_BLOCKED here, but it is served from the repo's docs/ folder (index.html, download.html, yearly release notes 2013.html-2026.html, help/), and its simd.sourceforge.net mirror, which was reachable, links no benchmark or comparison report, so the blocked pages do not hide numbers. The OpenCV resize special test (built only with SIMD_OPENCV, matching OpenCV's thread count to Simd's) exists in src/Test/TestResize.cpp but its results are not published; ResizeOpenCv always calls cv::resize with the default interpolation regardless of the Simd method under test. Web searches found no third-party Simd versus OpenCV or libyuv benchmark (a search snippet from a stereo-vision course repo on git.tdem.in reports SIMD 3.54x faster than OpenCV, snippet only and not opened; it does not name this library).

notes: Notable (2.3k stars, vcpkg) but no numbers against any baseline; keep at D and record 'no published baseline comparison'. The earlier caveat about blocked pages is resolved: the pages are the repo's docs/ folder, mirrored on simd.sourceforge.net, with no benchmarks.
